items.title: Nuit de la RPP: voici les consignes de sécurité
items.description: Ce texte fait part des consignes de sécurité à l’occasion de la Nuit de la Révolution Progressiste et Populaire (RPP) qui aura lieu dans la soirée du mercredi 30 septembre 2026. CONSIGNES DE SÉCURITÉ DE LA NUIT DE LA RPP À l’occasion de la Nuit de la Révolution, chaque participant est invité à faire preuve de vigilance, de responsabilité et de civisme afin de contribuer au bon déroulement de l’événement. DOCUMENTS ET EFFETS PERSONNELS Avoir sur soi une pièce d’identité valide ainsi que les documents afférents à son engin (moto ou véhicule) ; Éviter de venir avec de gros sacs ou des objets de valeur ; Éviter de venir sur le site avec armes ou tout autre objet dangereux. DÉPLACEMENTS ET STATIONNEMENT Porter le casque à moto, respecter le Code de la route et les consignes des agents chargés de la circulation ; Garer les engins uniquement dans les parkings indiqués et gardés ; Verrouiller les véhicules et ne laisser aucun objet de valeur visible à l’intérieur. ACCÈS ET CONTRÔLES DE SÉCURITÉ Se soumettre aux contrôles des FDS et des agents habilités. Respecter les files, barrières, points d’accès et voies réservées aux secours. Ne pas tenter de contourner les dispositifs de sécurité ou d’accéder aux zones interdites. VIGILANCE SUR LE SITE Signaler immédiatement aux FDS ou aux organisateurs toute situation, personne ou objet suspect ; Éviter de relayer des rumeurs ou fausses alertes susceptibles de provoquer un mouvement de panique. ENFANTS ET PERSONNES VULNÉRABLES Dans la mesure du possible, éviter de venir avec les enfants en bas âge compte tenu de la forte affluence ; Maintenir les enfants sous surveillance permanente ; En cas de perte d’un proche, prévenir immédiatement les agents de sécurité. TENUE Éviter les tenues dépravées ; Éviter les chaussures à talons hauts. SANTÉ ET SECOURS En cas de malaise ou d’accident, alerter immédiatement les secours et faciliter leur intervention ; Ne pas stationner ni laisser de véhicule sur les voies d’accès réservées aux secours. PARKINGS Maison du peuple Espace Saint Léon Siège FESPACO Terrain USO Terrain cité An III NUMÉROS D’URGENCE En cas d’urgence ou pour signaler une situation suspecte, contacter : 16, 17, 18, 10 10 et 80 00 11 45. La sécurité est l’affaire de tous. Restons donc vigilants, respectons les consignes des Forces de Défense et de Sécurité et facilitons l’intervention des services de secours. Ensemble, faisons de la Nuit de la Révolution un moment de rassemblement, de convivialité et surtout de sécurité. Par Wakat Séra L’article Nuit de la RPP: voici les consignes de sécurité est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: «Primitive Robot» | Concert de Marcondiro à Tunis
items.description: Marcondiro, un groupe de musique rock indépendant et d'auteur, fondé à Rome en 2009 par le chanteur et performeur Marco Borrelli, présente sa démarche artistique à Tunis, le jeudi 1 er octobre à 20 heures, sur la scène de L’Agora à La Marsa. Il présentera «Primitive Robot», aux côtés de Valerio Cesarini et du musicien tunisien Ziad Trabelsi. Le rendez-vous s'inscrit dans le cadre de la 34 e édition du Festival Sete Sóis Sete Luas, manifestation internationale qui, depuis plus de trente ans, favorise à travers la musique et la culture le dialogue entre les pays méditerranéens et le monde lusophone. A Tunis, il prend la forme d’une rencontre artistique qui dépasse la simple dimension du concert : des langages, des origines et des sensibilités différentes entrent en dialogue dans l’un des cadres internationaux qui ont fait de l’échange culturel leur identité. Au cœur de la soirée se trouvera l’univers de «Primitive Robot» , un projet dans lequel Marcondiro met en tension deux dimensions en apparence opposées : le primitif et le technologique. Une contradiction qui devient matière musicale et narrative et qui interroge le rapport de l’homme contemporain à ses origines, à la machine et à une réalité en transformation toujours plus rapide. À Tunis, cette recherche prend une dimension supplémentaire grâce à la rencontre avec Ziad Trabelsi, musicien tunisien, et à la présence de Valerio Cesarini. Le concert devient ainsi un espace de croisement où l’écriture et la vision de Marcondiro se confrontent à d’autres sonorités et traditions, au sein d’un même espace géographique méditerranéen. «Amener Primitive Robot à Tunis, c’est une nouvelle fois le faire sortir de ses frontières et le mettre en relation avec un autre lieu, une autre culture, une autre manière de ressentir la musique» , souligne Marcondiro.Il ajoute : «La Méditerranée est depuis toujours un espace où les identités ne restent pas immobiles : elles se rencontrent, se mélangent et évoluent. Jouer avec Ziad et Valerio dans le cadre du Sete Sóis Sete Luas, c’est entrer pleinement dans ce mouvement.» Créé il y a 34 ans, le Festival Sete Sóis Sete Luas représente en 2026 un réseau culturel international fondé sur la circulation des artistes, la création originale et la rencontre entre les cultures. L’étape tunisienne offre ainsi à Primitive Robot une nouvelle dimension internationale et, surtout, un terrain en cohérence avec la nature même du projet : faire de la musique un espace où des identités en apparence éloignées peuvent se reconnaître, se transformer et donner naissance à quelque chose de nouveau. L’article «Primitive Robot» | Concert de Marcondiro à Tunis est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Manchester City's Premier League charges: What comes next?
items.description: Manchester City’s fate in a legal battle with the Premier League is yet to be sealed, but reports they have been found guilty on widespread financial misconduct have sparked speculation of what comes next. The dominant Premier League force for more than a decade, swingeing sanctions against City would send shockwaves through English football. Rival clubs are set to launch their own legal action seeking hundreds of millions of pounds in compensation, while there is debate over whether some of City’s many titles and trophies over the past 15 years could be stripped. AFP Sports looks at the next steps and potential fall out from the case: Sanction and appeals process The Athletic first reported on Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they faced. However, no sanction has yet been approved. Even once a decision is made on how City will be punished, should they be found guilty, the club are almost certain to appeal. In a letter to City fans on Saturday, the club’s chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said: “Our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.” A case that began after German outlet Der Spiegel published leaked documents from City executives in 2018, could still take a lengthy time to fully resolve. According to Premier League rules, the sanction can vary from a points deduction, a fine or even expulsion from the division. Everton and Nottingham Forest were handed points deductions in the 2023/24 season for single breaches of financial sustainability rules. On that basis, City would face almost certain relegation if found guilty of over 100 charges. Whether the sanction is applied before an appeal is heard will be another bone of contention. If it is, City could face relegation before overturning any guilty verdict. On the other hand, if City, who currently sit top of the table, are not punished until after an appeal, it could cost other clubs their place in the top-flight or lucrative European qualification. Even after the Premier League process if over, there is also the chance that City’s Abu Dhabi-backed owners seek redress in England’s High Court if they challenge a legal issue regarding how the arbitration process was conducted. Who stands to gain? City’s rivals were quick to revel in the news of their potential demise. “Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet,” posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team to finish second to City in the 2011/12 season. The reality is that stripping and retroactively awarding titles is a messy process. City’s charges relate to the period between 2009 and 2018. In that time they won four league titles, with United and Liverpool twice finishing second in those seasons. Yet City have won another four since, arguably built on foundations that were fraudulently gained. They also won four League Cups and one FA Cup, the club’s first trophy for 35 years, in the period between 2009 and 2018. “I don’t seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either,” Tony Pulis, whose Stoke side lost the 2011 FA Cup final to City, told the BBC . “A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely. But I still feel cheated.” A more likely source of recompense for clubs that missed out is through financial compensation. In June, Everton were told they must pay Burnley 35 million ($46 million) after they edged out the Clarets to Premier League survival in the same season they broke financial sustainability rules. What about City’s stars? Less than a month ago, City completed the biggest ever transfer spend in one window, splashing out around 460m on the likes of Enzo Fernandez, Elliott Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi. The impending verdict on the charges has to this point made little impact on City’s ability to attract and retain their star names. Talismanic striker Erling Haaland signed a nine-year contract in 2025 that could keep him tied down till his 34th birthday. How many, if any, of the players managed to negotiate exit clauses in the case City were heavily sanctioned remains to be seen.

items.title: REMA 2026 : Le festival revient du 22 au 25 octobre prochain avec un « Focus Burkina » et un Forum IA
items.description: La 9e édition des Rencontres musicales africaines (REMA) se tiendra du 22 au 25 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, sous le thème « Followers, de passifs à actifs ». L’annonce a été faite ce lundi 28 septembre 2026 lors d’une conférence de presse. Durant quatre jours, les REMA réuniront artistes, professionnels de la musique et acteurs du numérique autour d’échanges, de rencontres et de célébrations de la musique africaine. Selon le promoteur des REMA, l’artiste musicien Salif Naaba, cette édition vise notamment à transformer les followers en véritables consommateurs de contenus et de produits culturels. « Il s’agit de passer d’un simple follower passif à un follower actif, qui assiste aux concerts, achète, streame les morceaux et participe véritablement à la vie de l’artiste », a-t-il expliqué. Le promoteur des ReMA a également ajouté que cette édition 2026 sera entièrement dédiées à la jeunesse. Selon lui, la programmation entend ainsi accorder une place importante aux jeunes artistes, étudiants, producteurs, managers et autres acteurs de la filière musicale. Une vue des participants Des conférences et rencontres professionnelles sont notamment prévues les 23 et 24 octobre au Centre culturel du Faso. L'artiste Alif Naaba, a par ailleurs invité la jeunesse a sortir nombreux pour cet événement. Pour sa part, la cheffe des partenariats de l’Union européenne au Burkina Faso, Inga Stefanowicz, a salué le partenariat avec les REMA. Selon elle, l’Union européenne accompagne pour la troisième fois cette initiative qui contribue à la promotion et à la professionnalisation du secteur culturel et musical, particulièrement au profit de la jeunesse. Inga Stefanowicz, Cheffe des partenariats de l’Union européenne au Burkina Faso, La représentante de l'Union Européenne a également souligné l’importance accordée à la jeunesse dans les actions de l’Union européenne, notamment à travers la création d’emplois et la professionnalisation des métiers culturels. Cette édition sera marquée par plusieurs innovations, notamment la fusion de la REMA Welcome Night et de la cérémonie d’ouverture en une grande soirée de lancement, ainsi que le « Focus Burkina », consacré à la découverte et à la valorisation des artistes burkinabè. Un Forum IA abordera également l’impact de l’intelligence artificielle sur la création musicale, les métiers de la filière, les usages et la protection des droits. Deux grandes soirées de concerts live sont également prévues du vendredi 23 et samedi 24 octobre. Le Centre culturel du Faso accueillera le REMA Space, un espace dédié aux rencontres et à la création. Pour faciliter l’accès aux informations et l’achat des billets, une application dénommée « Remapp » a été mise en place. Le ticket d’entrée est fixé à 1 000 F CFA. Sakinatou ZOUNDI Minute.bf

items.title: French teens blockade schools as unions vow day of 'anger' over cost-cutting budget
items.description: French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of some high schools that has angered the government, with unions planning nationwide protests over a cost-cutting budget. High school students have since last week staged protests outside their schools over issues including timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers, with some blocking entrances with rubbish bins and setting fire to them. The movement in the lycees, which handle the final years of school in France, started in the Ile-de-France region around Paris, where blockades in some 10 schools were reported by education authorities Tuesday. It has now spread to other cities nationwide. Masked students gathered outside the Lycee Cesar Baggio in Lille, in northern France, as a bin burned, with police using teargas as clashes erupted, an AFP photographer said. A placard which reads “Macron explosion” is seen in front of the entrance of the Lycee Arago high school blocked by French high school students in Paris as part of a day of strikes and protests by public sector workers, including firefighters, in France, on September 29, 2026. — Reuters Teens piled up dozens of bins to prevent entrance to the Lycee Gabriel Guist’hau in the western city of Nantes, while in Paris there was an uneasy standoff between 30 students and a contingent of police at the Arago school. Similar actions were also reported in cities including Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast. Nationwide demonstrations At the Lamartine school in Paris around 80 students gathered outside brandishing slogans including “more hours of lessons than sleep” and “8am to 6pm, are we pupils or under arrest?” The actions came as unions planned a day of nationwide demonstrations and also strikes over the budget of Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu , a close ally of President Emmanuel Macron. Tens of thousands were expected to rally in Paris and other cities, with teachers and fire services striking nationwide although with public transport not badly affected. “The anger is immense. I warn the government — it must address the demands and revise the draft budget, which is dangerous for the country and is driving us straight into the wall of recession at 200 kilometres an hour,” the head of the hardline CGT union Sophie Binet told BFM TV . A 17-year-old pupil at the Lamartine school, who asked not to be named, said they had been angered by a lack of resources, overheated classrooms and overly congested timetables. “We are also there to support our teachers who have a crazy amount of work compared to what they earn,” she told AFP . French police walk past the entrance of the Lycee Arago high school blocked by French high school students in Paris as part of a day of strikes and protests by public sector workers, including firefighters, in France, on September 29, 2026. — Reuters Lecornu on Monday said any escalation of demonstrations at high schools would be “irresponsible” and lashed out at the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party for encouraging the protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 164 arrests took place on Monday and 180 schools were affected, adding: “We cannot tolerate excesses.”

items.title: Lahore court grants police 6-day remand of two suspects in Azeri woman's gang-rape case
items.description: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday allowed Defence C police a six-day physical remand of two suspects in a case against them over the alleged gang-rape of an Azeri woman. The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday. One of the prime suspects had been arrested on Monday, while another’s arrest surfaced on Tuesday. According to Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Zeeshan Raza, police had identified the third suspect and were conducting raids to trace him. On Tuesday, the police produced the two arrested men before Magistrate Azhar Mahmood at Cantonment Courts. The investigating officer sought their 14-day physical remand for interrogation, collection of evidence and DNA examination. However, the magistrate approved a six-day physical remand of the suspects. Separately, a session’s court granted interim pre-arrest bail to a female suspect in the case, restraining police from arresting her till Oct 5. The Azeri woman had mentioned in her application to the police that two women had approached her for dinner and later they went to a cafe, where the three men accused of raping her had met them. One of the two women who allegedly approached the victim appeared before the court along with her lawyer on Tuesday. The lawyer argued that his client had been implicated in the case with mala fide intention. He said she wanted to join police investigation to prove her innocence. He further expressed fear that she would be arrested and requested the court to approve are pre-arrest bail. The court granted the suspect bail till Oct 5, with the directive to join the police investigation before the next hearing. Woman says suspects told her to drink alcohol The judicial proceedings came a day after the foreign woman recorded her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). Police Sub-Inspector Faryal Malik, the investigating officer, had produced the woman before the magistrate under strict security arrangements. In her statement, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the woman said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore. “I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said. According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other. The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand on Tuesday (first suspect). Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man. According to the complainant, in a separate room, one of the women took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the second woman also joined them. The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room. When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money. The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go. She alleged that the three men raped her. She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police. According to her statement, the suspects also took her handbag containing Rs200,000, an iPhone 13 Pro Max and another mobile phone. She then requested some people present there to help her call the police emergency number 15, following which the police arrived. The case The Defence C police had registered a case against three unidentified suspects on Sept 26 on the woman’s complaint. Police had also taken two close relatives and a domestic servant of one of the suspects into custody. The vehicle allegedly used in the incident had also been taken into custody. On Sunday, Lahore police had requested federal authorities to place the names of the three prime suspects in the case on the Provisional National Identification List (PNIL), saying they had fled Lahore shortly after the alleged assault. It is the second such case in which a foreign woman was reportedly gang-raped in the Defence C police station area during the last four months. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.
